crime_highlights: Mr. Miller had made his way back to the residence and was coming up the stairs with a rifle in his hand
while Mr. Miller had the rifle in his hand, he made remarks of a threatening nature toward Mr. Douglas
Mr. Miller had the rifle in his hand and subsequently a shot was fired
The complainant heard a loud bang and observed drywall dust in the air near where he was located. He noted holes in the wall and ceiling of the room, at the front of the house.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Miller is the product of intergenerational and Residential School trauma
the unique systemic and background factors which may have played a part in bringing the particular Aboriginal offender before the courts
may bear on the culpability of the offender, to the extent that they shed light on his or her level of moral blameworthiness
consideration must be given to the unique systemic and background factors that play a part in bringing Indigenous offenders before the court
note: Court never states Gladue factors reduced this sentence; exceptional circumstances rest on rehabilitation.

crime_highlights: Mr. Gerow threw or pushed Mr. Nelmes off the railing of the deck of Mr. Gerow's home
Mr. Nelmes dropped approximately 11 feet to the ground, seriously injuring his back and pelvis
Mr. Nelmes has not fully recovered from his injuries and is unlikely to do so
rationale_highlights: the cultural disruption of Indigenous communities through programs such as residential schools has caused broad, generalized impacts in communities, including intergenerational trauma
In Mr. Gerow's case, the impact can be seen in his disconnect from his community and extended family until he was well into adulthood
alienation from community and severing of family ties are the most significant Gladue factors to take into account in sentencing Mr. Gerow
I have considered the intergenerational impacts on them which may result from the incarceration of Mr. Gerow
I find that a sentence which minimizes disruption to Mr. Gerow's ability to care for his family is appropriate
